title: Total degree of the exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ polynomial
statement:
Let $p$ be a prime and fix natural numbers $\mathrm{vars}$ and $\mathrm{width}$. Let $P_0,\dots,P_{\mathrm{width}-1}$ be polynomials in $\mathrm{vars}$ variables over the field $\bbz/p$. Then the total degree of the exact $\mathrm{MOD}_p$ polynomial $1 - \bigl(\sum_i P_i\bigr)^{p-1}$ is at most
\[
(p-1)\cdot \sup_i \deg(P_i),
\]
the supremum being taken over all $i$ (and read as $0$ when $\mathrm{width}=0$).
hypotheses_covered: vars and width are natural numbers
a family of width polynomials P_i in vars variables over Z/p
replaced:
The total degree of $\texttt{ACP.exactMod}$ applied to $P_1,\dots,P_{\mathrm{width}}$ is at
most $(p-1)\cdot \sup_i \deg(P_i)$.
